news.title: Smart Communications powers unforgettable FIFA World Cup viewing parties across Kampai, Nolita Joe’s and Scratch
news.lede: Football fans found more than just a place to watch the game—they found the party. Across the two FIFA World Cup semifinal matches and the highly anticipated final, Smart Communications, as co-presenter, teamed up with Kampai, Nolita Joe’s, and Scratch to transform match nights into one of the city’s most exciting football celebrations. The three venues welcomed hundreds of football fans, bringing together great food, flowing drinks, music, and an electric atmosphere that lasted until the final whistle. What made the experience stand out was its Double Party Concept—starting with a late-night pre-game party complete with DJs, cocktails, and football-themed activities before seamlessly transitioning into the live match screenings.

news.title: Klopp named new head coach of Germany men's football team
news.lede: Germany has turned to Jürgen Klopp to lead a new era for the four-time world champions after their disappointing World Cup exit, with hopes of building toward future international tournaments. The German Football Association (DFB) has appointed Jürgen Klopp as the new head coach of the national team on Friday, ending speculation about who would succeed Julian Nagelsmann. DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said the association's governing bodies had unanimously approved Klopp's appointment, describing him as the "ideal choice" for the role. "It is a great honor to sit here today," Klopp said at the press conference announcing his appointment, adding he was "delighted."

news.title: Argentina forced to make change as FIFA ruling emerges after World Cup final
news.lede: Argentina are set to be given another brutal reminder of their devastating World Cup final defeat. The thuggish and negative tactics employed by Lionel Scaloni's side proved in vain as Spain clinched a deserved victory thanks to Ferran Torres's extra-time strike. Argentina had been aiming to lift the trophy for the fourth time in their history after Lionel Messi inspired the team to glory at Qatar 2022. Since becoming world champions, their strip had featured a gold crest displaying an outline of the trophy alongside the words "FIFA World Champions 2022".

news.title: 23 million sign petition demanding Argentina's lifetime ban from World Cup
news.lede: The appeal, titled 'Argentina Out,' drew a ridiculous 23,316,108 signatures from 170 countries worldwide. An initial target of five million was set by organisers, but the final total blew past that to become one of the most circulated online petitions in history. Launched during the 2026 World Cup by irate football fans, it accused FIFA and match referees of 'bias' towards Argentina and captain Lionel Messi, something FIFA strongly denied. "Why should the rest of the teams play in the tournament if the winner is known in advance?"

news.title: Loewe celebrates Spain's second World Cup with a commemorative photo collection
news.lede: Madrid – The Spanish national team's historic victory in the 2026 FIFA World Cup has dominated the news all week, including within the fashion sector. To celebrate this well-deserved triumph, Spanish house Loewe has released a collection of photographs by creative Hannah Coen. Coen, a London-based creative, has a well-established career in fashion, regularly collaborating with brands such as Paul Smith, Camperlab, Ferragamo and Loewe. She first worked with the historic Spanish house this past April 2026, on the launch of its 180th anniversary campaign.

news.title: Messiah or papering over cracks? Klopp must sway doubters in Germany rebuild
news.lede: Klopp has signed a four-year deal as Germany head coach. He was once hailed as Liverpool's footballing messiah. Now Jurgen Klopp has been asked to work miracles for his country. Last month, Klopp watched on as a touchline TV pundit as Germany went out of the World Cup in a shock penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay.

news.title: FIFA announce World Cup team of the tournament as baffled fans say 'what a joke'
news.lede: FIFA's fan-voted World Cup dream XI does not feature Golden Glove winner Unai Simon or Young Player Award recipient Pau Cubarsi. Vozinha is in goal with almost 40% of the votes, while Dayot Upemecano and Lisandro Martinez are the two central defenders chosen by fans. Of those two, the France international received the most votes, with nearly 15%, while his defensive partner in this team barely managed 10%. The two full-backs selected are Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro, both of Spain.
